name: Transformer foundations
description: A small, inspectable decoder-only transformer. An educational architecture, not a trained checkpoint.
documentation: Start at the architecture overview, then open a block or inspect an edge. Symbolic axes are B (batch), T (current query positions), S (visible key positions), D (hidden width), Hq (query heads), Hkv (KV heads), Dh (features per head), F (FFN width), V (vocabulary) and L (layers). The workbench computes exact dimensions and a real demo BPE trace. Attention probabilities are synthetic examples; no trained model weights are loaded. Optional memory and MTP views illustrate separate architecture extensions. Model definitions, equations, citations, notes, positions and viewports travel together in this versioned JSON document.

tokenizer.description: Deterministic byte-level BPE with a small explicit vocabulary. No pre-tokenization, Unicode normalization or special tokens. See src/model/tokenizer.ts.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention

graphs.title: The architecture, unfolded.
graphs.subtitle: One prompt. Every transformation.
graphs.description: A decoder-only teaching architecture with RoPE, pre-normalization, grouped-query attention, and SwiGLU. Optional memory and MTP branches are shown explicitly; this is not a named production model.

nodes.title: Tokenization
nodes.subtitle: Text → discrete token IDs
nodes.description: Encode text as UTF-8 bytes, apply ranked byte-pair merges, and look up integer token IDs. Inspect the actual merge trace in the tokenizer lab.
notes: The bundled tokenizer is a small, lossless teaching BPE vocabulary. It is not the tokenizer of a production model.

nodes.title: Token embeddings
nodes.subtitle: A learned vector for every token
nodes.description: Gather one learned embedding row per token ID. This is an indexed lookup, not multiplication of token IDs by the weight matrix.

nodes.title: Transformer blocks
nodes.subtitle: Attention + feed-forward + residuals
nodes.description: Pass the residual stream through L distinct decoder blocks. Each block has its own parameters and KV state. Open one block to follow its two residual paths.

nodes.title: KV cache
nodes.subtitle: Persistent state · every layer
nodes.description: Keep previously computed keys and values for attention. Every layer writes only its own state. Query heads share KV heads according to the selected attention architecture.

nodes.title: N-gram memory
nodes.subtitle: Optional · conditional lookup
nodes.description: A separate, optional memory module retrieves learned vectors from local token n-grams. Inspect an illustrative hash lookup and gated fusion pathway.
notes: An extension study, not a claim that all transformers contain n-gram memory.

nodes.title: Multi-token prediction
nodes.subtitle: Optional · additional future targets
nodes.description: Auxiliary prediction modules provide additional training targets. Open a sequential MTP pathway to see shifted token embeddings and the shared output head.

nodes.title: Output head & sampling
nodes.subtitle: Normalize → logits → next token
nodes.description: Normalize final hidden vectors, project them to vocabulary logits, select a token and decode its bytes. Open this pathway to inspect each operation.

nodes.title: Self-attention
nodes.subtitle: Mix information across tokens

nodes.title: SwiGLU feed-forward
nodes.subtitle: Expand → gate → contract
nodes.description: Compute two D→F projections, apply SiLU to the gate branch, multiply element by element, and project F→D. Open the feed-forward graph for each matrix.
notes: This dense FFN can be replaced by a mixture-of-experts subgraph in a future model definition.

graphs.title: Attention, operation by operation.
graphs.subtitle: Follow a query. Inspect every head.
graphs.description: Dense causal attention with configurable MHA, GQA, or MQA sharing. Prefill processes the full prompt; decode processes one new query against a longer cached prefix.

nodes.title: Normalized hidden state
nodes.subtitle: One vector per query position
nodes.description: Input to the layer’s learned query, key and value projections.

nodes.title: Query projection
nodes.subtitle: X · Wq → reshape heads
nodes.description: Multiply by the query weight matrix and reshape to expose the query-head axis.

nodes.title: Key projection
nodes.subtitle: X · Wk → reshape KV heads
nodes.description: Project keys using Hkv heads. Sharing reduces this projection and its persistent cache.

nodes.title: Value projection
nodes.subtitle: X · Wv → reshape KV heads
nodes.description: Values carry the features that attention will average. This architecture applies RoPE to Q and K, not V.

nodes.title: RoPE · queries
nodes.subtitle: Rotate feature pairs by position
nodes.description: Rotate pairs of query features using their absolute token positions. Decode positions continue from the cached prefix.

nodes.title: RoPE · keys
nodes.subtitle: Rotate, then append to cache
nodes.description: Use the same position-dependent rotations for the newly computed keys.

nodes.title: Key cache
nodes.subtitle: Append along sequence axis
nodes.description: Persist rotated keys for this layer. Prior keys are reused; they are not recomputed for every generated token.

nodes.title: Value cache
nodes.subtitle: Append along sequence axis
nodes.description: Persist values independently from keys, with the same layer, batch, head and sequence indexing.

nodes.title: Q · Kᵀ
nodes.subtitle: Pairwise query–key dot products
nodes.description: For each query head, select its KV group and contract over Dh. The result has a query-position axis and a key-position axis.
notes: g(h) = floor(h / (Hq/Hkv)) for zero-based, contiguous query-head groups.

nodes.title: Scale + causal mask
nodes.subtitle: Divide by √Dh · mask the future
nodes.description: Scale the dot products, then add negative infinity wherever the key position is in the future. Decode uses absolute positions, not a naïve T×S triangular mask starting at zero.

nodes.title: Row-wise softmax
nodes.subtitle: Normalize over key positions
nodes.description: For every query position and query head, turn visible scores into non-negative weights that sum to one. Masked positions receive zero weight.
notes: Subtracting each row’s maximum m improves numerical stability.

nodes.title: Attention · V
nodes.subtitle: Weighted sum over visible values
nodes.description: Contract the key-position axis S. Each query head produces Dh features using the V head assigned to its KV group.

nodes.title: Concatenate heads
nodes.subtitle: Transpose + reshape
nodes.description: Move the head axis next to features and flatten Hq×Dh. Concatenation rearranges features; it does not sum heads.

nodes.title: Output projection
nodes.subtitle: Joined heads · Wo
nodes.description: Mix the concatenated head features and return D features to the attention residual branch.
notes: FlashAttention computes the same dense attention with tiled kernels; it need not materialize the full attention matrix. The heatmap here is synthetic teaching data.

graphs.subtitle: Layer × batch × KV head × sequence × features.
graphs.description: A logical tensor view of persistent attention state. Inspect a layer and KV head below. Physical allocations may use blocks, strides, quantization, sharding or paging.

nodes.title: Persistent K tensor
nodes.subtitle: Write only the current layer slice
nodes.description: Append keys at the correct sequence positions. The logical all-layer view has axes L, B, Hkv, S, Dh; implementations often store separate tensors per layer.

nodes.title: Persistent V tensor
nodes.subtitle: A distinct allocation from K
nodes.description: Store values with the same logical indexing as keys. The K/V selector is not an extra attention head.

nodes.title: Attend to the prefix
nodes.subtitle: Read this layer’s K and V
nodes.description: A query reads visible positions from its assigned KV head. Query heads never share state across decoder layers.
notes: Logical dense cache bytes = 2 × L × B × Hkv × S × Dh × bytes per scalar. Allocator overhead and quantization metadata are excluded.
PagedAttention changes physical memory management, not the meaning of these logical axes.
MLA requires a different state schema: compressed latent vectors plus positional key state, rather than this full K/V representation.

graphs.title: From hidden states to text.
graphs.subtitle: Normalize. Project. Select. Decode.
graphs.description: The standard next-token output pathway, including the final normalization, vocabulary projection, selection policy and byte decoding.

nodes.title: Final RMSNorm
nodes.subtitle: Normalize the residual stream
nodes.description: Normalize each token vector over its feature dimension before the vocabulary projection. RMSNorm scales by root mean square without subtracting the feature mean.

nodes.title: Vocabulary projection
nodes.subtitle: Hidden state → logits
nodes.description: Project the final hidden state into one logit per vocabulary item. During generation only the last position is needed. The embedding and output weights may be tied, but that is an architecture choice.

nodes.title: Select next token
nodes.subtitle: Temperature · softmax · sampling
nodes.description: Convert last-position logits into a distribution, optionally filter with top-k or top-p, then choose a token. Greedy decoding uses argmax. Temperature must be positive for the softmax formula.
notes: This workbench visualizes structure. It does not run trained weights or generate language.

nodes.title: Decode to text
nodes.subtitle: Token bytes → UTF-8 text
nodes.description: Map the selected IDs back to bytes and decode the concatenated byte stream. Append the chosen token ID to the model sequence for the next inference step.
notes: Output is detokenization, not re-encoding. Some byte-level tokens are not valid UTF-8 individually.

edges.label: matrix product
edges.operation: Multiply normalized hidden vectors by the vocabulary projection.
edges.description: Multiply normalized hidden vectors by the vocabulary projection.

edges.label: last position
edges.operation: Slice the last time position before generation.
edges.description: Slice the last time position before generation.

edges.label: token ID
edges.operation: Decode the selected vocabulary ID.
edges.description: Decode the selected vocabulary ID.

graphs.title: Memory beyond the context.
graphs.subtitle: Bigrams, trigrams, four-grams.
graphs.description: An illustrative n-gram conditional-memory path inspired by Engram, with a simple demonstration hash. This is an extension study rather than a full reproduction of Engram.

nodes.title: Causal n-gram windows
nodes.subtitle: Contiguous token IDs · n = 2, 3, 4
nodes.description: Construct token n-grams ending at the current position using only the available prefix. Do not look ahead to future tokens.

nodes.title: Hash addresses
nodes.subtitle: Deterministic sparse lookup
nodes.description: Map each n-gram to an address in a finite learned memory. Hash collisions are possible. The lab uses one FNV-style hash for illustration; Engram uses multiple heads and additional processing.

nodes.title: Retrieve embeddings
nodes.subtitle: Learned memory vectors
nodes.description: Gather trainable vectors at the hashed addresses. This is parameter memory, not stored attention keys and values.

nodes.title: Contextual hidden state
nodes.subtitle: Dynamic transformer features
nodes.description: The current hidden state controls whether retrieved local patterns should contribute.

nodes.title: Context-aware gated fusion
nodes.subtitle: Project + gate + residual
nodes.description: Project retrieved features to D and use a context-dependent gate before residual fusion. This equation is a simplified explanatory gate, not the complete Engram implementation.
notes: The full Engram design also includes tokenizer compression, multi-head hashing and a short convolution. Follow the source for exact architecture details.

edges.description: Hash a local token n-gram.

edges.description: Project retrieved embeddings before gating.

edges.description: Dynamic features condition the memory contribution.

graphs.title: Predict beyond the next token.
graphs.subtitle: An auxiliary training pathway.
graphs.description: A sequential MTP design inspired by DeepSeek-V3. The standard next-token head remains the main output path. Shifted ground-truth tokens feed the auxiliary modules during training.

nodes.title: Main-model hidden state
nodes.subtitle: At token position i
nodes.description: The backbone hidden state is the input to an auxiliary prediction depth.

nodes.title: Shifted token embedding
nodes.subtitle: Training: token i + k
nodes.description: At depth k, embed the shifted teacher-forced token using the shared embedding matrix. At inference, a proposed token takes this role.

nodes.title: Normalize + concatenate
nodes.subtitle: D + D → 2D → D
nodes.description: Normalize the previous-depth hidden state and the shifted embedding separately, concatenate them and project back to D.

nodes.title: MTP transformer block
nodes.subtitle: A depth-specific module
nodes.description: Transform the combined representation with its own causal block.

nodes.title: Shared output head
nodes.subtitle: Predict token i + k + 1
nodes.description: Apply the shared vocabulary projection and train against a further future target.

nodes.title: Auxiliary cross-entropy
nodes.subtitle: Average valid shifted positions
nodes.description: Compute the negative log-probability of the target and add weighted auxiliary losses to the main training objective. Invalid tail positions are excluded.
notes: Independent parallel heads are another MTP design. Sequential modules here are a distinct architecture choice.
Auxiliary modules can be discarded for ordinary inference or used for draft proposals with verification. They do not guarantee multiple accepted tokens per step.
